title: Hand X-ray for bone age
what: One X-ray picture of the hand is taken. From it, the doctor sees how mature your child's bones are.
why: When a child is growing too slowly or too fast, with early or late puberty, and during hormone treatment.
duration: the picture takes a couple of minutes; the report usually comes the same day or after a few days
tell_doctor: Your child's height and weight over the last years
Which hormones or medicines they take

prepare.title: Hands
prepare.text: Usually the left hand is X-rayed. Take off your child's rings and bracelets.

steps: Your child sits at a table
The hand is placed palm down on a plate
A protective apron is put on the body
Your child is asked to keep still for a couple of seconds
feel: They only need to sit still
after: The report usually comes the same day or after a few days
The doctor will compare bone age with real age and decide what comes next

faq.a: The dose is very small, since only the hand is X-rayed. A doctor orders it when the benefit is greater than the risk.

faq.q: What does it mean if the bone age is behind?
faq.a: It means the bones are maturing more slowly. The causes vary, and your doctor will explain.

reminders.text: X-ray of your child's hand tomorrow. Take off their rings and bracelets, and bring previous X-rays.
